detail: DECLARED observation: a side effect of MY OWN script on Sol's staged index, found by checking and fixed; reported so nobody finds it by surprise. What happened: my first eol-diffcheck.sh simulated Sol's re-stage by writing the fixed blob with GIT_OBJECT_DIRECTORY=<temp dir> GIT_ALTERNATE_OBJECT_DIRECTORIES=<real objects> git hash-object -w. Git FRESHENS (touches the mtime of) an identical object that already exists in an alternate instead of writing a new copy; I proved that in a scratch repo (mtime changed, nothing was written to the temp dir). I ran that script once against t114 at 02:27:07 WIB, and the mtime of the loose object file .git/objects/08/53fe017370aa61d6ae7971758b67c24ed7cb1c (Sol's staged blob 0853fe01, the version of tests/reporting/pr-33f.test.ts WITH the blank line) moved from 01:17:00 (when Sol staged) to 02:27:07. What did NOT change: the object's content and id (cat-file -t blob, 52533 bytes, rehash equals the id, git fsck clean, equals my cold backup of the staged bytes), the index file (raw sha256 7419f603f1e7a974119701250097ad4075ee335903b87d51aa30f1ac4c833403, identical at every check), the staged set, HEAD, any ref; the other nine staged blobs still show 01:17:00; no object was added or removed by it. Why it matters at all: the mtime of a loose object is read by git's pruning (gc --prune) and nothing else here, and a FRESHER mtime only makes an object live longer, never shorter. The script now writes into the temp object dir ONLY (no alternate while writing), reads through the alternate afterwards, and a measured pass of the corrected script leaves the mtime unchanged; the evidence run's own eol-diffcheck (02:34:35) did not move it again. I also ran a write-tree of Sol's index on a COPY at about 02:07 with GIT_OBJECT_DIRECTORY + alternates: that tree (e89733e3) was not in the real database, so nothing real was freshened. Separately, and NOT mine: the pi harness writes 'pi rewind' snapshot commits and a pack into this repository's object store (refs/pi-rewind/store) at its own times (01:00:39, 01:11:21, 01:16:20, 01:28:06, 01:44:30, 02:25:43). Everything else in this order used a PRIVATE COPY of the index (GIT_INDEX_FILE) for every ledger call, so the real index was never opened for writing by my commands.
